name: Qatari Nationality by Descent (Law No. 38 of 2005, Article 1.4) -- patrilineal

qualifying_event.description: A child is automatically Qatari, whether born in Qatar or abroad, if the father is a Qatari citizen. Citizenship by descent is patrilineal only under Law No. 38 of 2005 -- children of a Qatari mother and non-Qatari father do NOT acquire Qatari nationality automatically.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth certificate; father's Qatari nationality documentation.

requirements.blocker_text: Father is a Qatari citizen at the time of the child's birth (in Qatar or abroad). Having a Qatari MOTHER instead does not confer automatic citizenship under this law.

sources.title: American University in Cairo, Center for Migration and Refugee Studies -- verbatim English translation of Law No. 38 of 2005, Article 1.4: automatic citizenship for any child (born in Qatar or abroad) to a Qatari father; Article 2 'priority' language for naturalisation applicants with a Qatari mother affects queue position only, not automatic grant

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Qatar). STATUS: DRAFT -- same tier-2 sourcing caveat as the other Qatari citizenship files. GENDERED STRUCTURAL ASYMMETRY, THE MARQUEE FINDING FOR THIS FILE: descent-based citizenship is strictly PATRILINEAL. Children of Qatari WOMEN married to non-Qatari men do NOT acquire citizenship automatically -- this is not an oversight or a slower/harder path, it is a categorical exclusion under the primary law text. That population is instead the lead category in the 2018 Permanent Residency law's exemption list (see qa_permanent_residence.json's exempt_category group) -- they get settled status, never citizenship, through that route. This dataset does not treat the PR-law exemption as equivalent to citizenship by descent; they are modeled as two separate, unequal outcomes.
